correctness.rationale: Distance cannot decrease under deletion. For adjacent terminals the edge is compulsory. For nonadjacent terminals the original distance is two, so every geodesic has one intermediate vertex. A terminal intermediate is already dealt with by the compulsory edges; a nonterminal v forbids retaining both edges to any nonedge in G[L_v]. Thus the retained terminal neighbors form exactly a clique, independently at each nonterminal. Nonterminal-nonterminal deletions are free. This proves the polynomial and works when original nonterminal components or newly disconnected terminal pairs are present. Local maximum cliques minimize and count the minimum sets, while inclusion-maximal cliques give inclusion-minimal sets, with no free deletions. For example a cone on K2 disjoint union K1 has local maximal clique sizes 2 and 1. The cone on two triangles has e_T=6, d_v=6, local clique counts (1,6,6,2), hence z^9(z^3+6z^2+6z+2); the cubic's discriminant is -108. In the multipartite case a terminal part of size p_i>0 contributes one factor z^(p_i-1)(z+p_i) for every nonterminal outside it. Local maxima and maximal choices coincide (choose one from every available part); two optima differ by one edge swap exactly when they differ in one of these disjoint choice coordinates. The factors give nonpositive real zeros and the strictly stronger normalized Newton inequality gives strict log-concavity wherever three positive coefficients occur. For t>=3, three or more occupied parts already cost at least t compulsory edges. Two parts give pq>=p+q-1, with equality requiring one singleton terminal count and all nonterminals in the part with t-1 terminals. One terminal part costs (t-1) times the number of outside vertices. These cases give precisely stars, and a star realizes equality in each possible terminal placement.
residual_risks: The proof does not depend on finite census coverage. The multipartite supplementary checker iterates a finite family with an edge-count cap, not every order-six instance. The result does not cover original terminal distances above two or assert star-only equality for two terminals.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The novelty is the exact decomposition with its explicit counting and rigidity consequences, not general transversal theory or Newton's inequalities. Once the decomposition is established some of the displayed corollaries are elementary.

evidence: Semi-cutting here means hitting every geodesic of every terminal pair, per Lemma 2.6. After compulsory deletions the equivalent local problem is vertex cover in the graph on the incident terminal edges whose forbidden pairs are nonedges of G[L_v]; its surviving complements are cliques. The edge-geodesic-transversal problem hits maximal geodesics of the whole graph, which is not that family.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The equivalence supplies the starting formulation, not an already stated reduction and enumerator for this diameter class. The maximal-geodesic polynomial concerns a different collection of constraints.

value.rationale: Counting all size classes is a natural refinement of the published semi-cutting minimization question. The factorization tells a future researcher exactly which local graph invariants control every coefficient and optimum, and the cone construction explains why real-rootedness from the bipartite or multipartite cases cannot persist under just the terminal diameter condition. The multipartite result describes all optima and their exchange graph, and tests sharpness of the published bound for each placement rather than merely reproducing that bound.
residual_risks: It is a structural enumeration, not a polynomial-time algorithm for computing arbitrary clique polynomials or a result at larger terminal diameters.
